modern: Practise even the things which you despair of accomplishing. For even the left hand, which is ineffective for all other things for lack of practice, holds the bridle more firmly than the right hand; for it has been practised in this.
original: Practise thyself even in the things which thou despairest of accomplishing. For even the left hand, which is ineffectual for all other things for want of practice, holds the bridle more vigorously than the right hand; for it has been practised in this.
notification: Practise even the things which you despair of accomplishing.
notification_original: Practise thyself even in the things which thou despairest of accomplishing.

explained.summary: Keep practising even what you think you’ll never manage. Marcus’s example is the left hand: clumsy at most tasks, yet it holds a horse’s reins more firmly than the right, simply because that’s the job it has been trained for. Skill comes from repetition, not from natural talent.
explained.today: Learning a language at forty, playing the guitar with stiff fingers, or staying patient with a teenager can all feel hopeless at first. They’re like the left hand on the reins: awkward until you’ve done it enough times that it becomes the thing you’re steadiest at.
